headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and cascading errors; shared write access also creates medium data-leakage and capability-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the user filesystem and uses clipboard/stdin-stdout, while transformers can ingest files and example scripts. Because A shares state via filesystem and B processes file content, attacker-controlled content from either side can be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented enough to judge, but the shared-file bridge makes injection plausible by default.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instructions into a file that agent_b later parses as input, injection is possible.
IF agent_b consumes untrusted file content produced by agent_a without provenance checks, prompt hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the agents.
Require provenance tags on all files passed from A to B.
Review any file before B ingests it.
Run A and B in separate directories.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can access the entire user filesystem and broad network egress; agent B can read files and call external services like Hugging Face Hub/transformers serve. In a shared workspace, sensitive local data touched by A can flow into B and then out through B's API calls or model-serving paths. This is a default-available leakage path, though not necessarily automatic.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, files read by A can be exposed to B.
IF B forwards file-derived content to Hugging Face Hub or a serving endpoint, local data can leave the machine.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for A and B.
Remove secrets from any shared directory.
Disable outbound network for B during file review.
Inspect files before passing them between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and subprocess/shell capability, and A explicitly shares state via filesystem. That creates a direct race on mutable files, git state, and generated artifacts with no locking primitive documented. The overlap is enough for destructive overwrite or inconsistent outputs in default use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
IF both modify the same git repository without locks, commits or working tree state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git branches per agent.
Check for file locks before writes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate shell commands and file edits, and B can consume files and act through APIs or serving workflows. If B treats A's outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts from A can cascade into B's downstream actions without verification. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced files or text as authoritative input, unverified errors can propagate.
IF A emits commands or facts that B executes or renders, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step in B for all A-produced facts.
Limit A to draft-only outputs.
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A touches anything reachable on the local machine and handles model-provider API keys, while B touches multimodal data and can call external APIs. If regulated or sensitive local data is present, the pair can move it into third-party services without a documented residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF local regulated data is present in files A can read, it may be processed by external model providers.
IF B sends user content to Hugging Face services, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Review retention settings for model providers.
Use redacted sample data.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
